title: Iron Ore Supply and Demand (Commission of Inquiry) Bill 2015
short_title: Iron Ore Supply and Demand (Commission of Inquiry) Bill 2015

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would establish a judicial commission to investigate iron ore supply and demand, including production increases, effects on competitors and Australian tax revenue.
The commission would examine production decisions and possible measures to reduce output, using powers to summon witnesses, obtain evidence, hold hearings and seek search warrants.
It would report to Parliament within three months, commence the day after Royal Assent and be funded through appropriations for ordinary government services.
changes: New offences would cover misleading evidence, document destruction, witness interference and contempt.
Legal or financial assistance could be provided to people appearing before the commission.
Suspected offences identified during the inquiry could be referred to the relevant enforcement authority.
summary.affected: Iron ore producing companies whose production increases the inquiry would examine, people summoned as witnesses, and the Commissioner and staff of the Commission are affected.
